doc.title: Plas Johnson interviewed by Monk Rowe, Sarasota, Florida, April 12, 1996

title: Becoming a studio player for film and TV
summary: Arrangers like Les Baxter, Billy May and Nelson Riddle used him as a soloist; work mushroomed from 1956 until the Beatles changed pop.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Studio work and jingles: New York session life

blocks.x: Tell us about studio work for film.

Well I had no plans of becoming a studio player it just kind of happened. The blues part of my playing got me on a lot of record dates, and my playing wasn’t all blues, you know I could play a pretty good ballad and follow changes and stuff like that and had a pretty good sound and I think one of the first arrangers to use me in that capacity, you know other than the blues stuff, was Les Baxter and maybe Van Alexander, Billy May, Nelson Riddle. I was being discovered by arrangers who used me in a solo capacity. Many times I’d go to a date and just play the solo and somebody else played the chart. It was kind of fun times.

Yeah. Kind of just from ‘56 on it kind of just mushroomed and I was quite busy between ‘56 and ‘62 or 3, up until the time maybe when the Beatles music came in and pop music changed entirely. But I was still busy because I did T.V. and movie stuff.
